sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 55:1
items.html: (to question) From the beginning to the end of the wisdom there is not even a single word that relates to any tangible or imaginary term, such as space, time, motion and so on. Also, there is no absence in spirituality, and any change of form does not mean that the first form is absent. Instead, the first form remains in its place, unchanged at all, and the disparity of form that has now been acquired is added to the first form. (The beginning of Inner Light)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 56:1
items.html: (to question) This language is a “language of branches” that points to their upper roots, since “You haven’t even a single blade of grass below that has not a root above.” Therefore, the sages of Kabbalah have found themselves a ready language to imply through the branches and to teach about their upper roots. (Inner Light, page 1, and the beginning of Inner Observation, the passage beginning “Beginning”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 57:1
items.html: (to question) Disparity of form distinguishes and separates the spirituals from one another. (Inner Light, item 30)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 58:1
items.html: (to question) The will to bestow in the upper light necessitates the existence of the will to receive in the emanated being. (Inner Observation, item 11, the passage beginning “And this is”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 59:1
items.html: (to question) Because of the form of the will to receive that was innovated with the upper light, since it wants to bestow, that innovated part that was innovated went out from the state of Emanator and came into the state of emanated being. (Inner Observation, item 11, the passage beginning “And this is,” and item 15, the passage beginning “And now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 60:1
items.html: (to question) The innovated form that emerged existence from absence, meaning the “will to receive” that is in every essence, is the “first substance” of every emanated being and every essence. Moreover, everything that exists in the emanated being or in the essence that is more than that substance, is regarded as light and abundance that is extended from the upper light “existence from existence,” and not at all as an emanated being and a created being. It is not surprising that a form becomes a substance, since it is so in corporeality as well. Our way is to determine the first form of the essence as the first substance because there is no attainment whatsoever in any matter in all of reality, since our senses perceive only incidents in the matter, which are forms that incarnate and come in the first substance. (Inner Observation, item 35, the passage beginning “Know”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 61:1
items.html: (to question) At the very beginning of the formation of the will to receive in the emanated being—called phase one of the desire—it has already departed the category of Emanator and become an emanated being. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 2, item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 62:1
items.html: (to question) There is no absence or loss in spirituality. The part that departs because of the disparity of form does not diminish or lessen the upper light at all. Rather, it is like lighting one candle from another, where the first is not lessened whatsoever. Thus, any change of form is an addition to the first. (Inner Observation, Part 2, regarding the integration of Ten Sefirot in every Sefira)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 63:1
items.html: (to question) All the multiplications and changes are done only by the impression and reception of His light in the vessels. However, the upper light in and of itself is in a state of complete rest, meaning unchanged and without any innovation. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 2, item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 64:1
items.html: (to question) There is no movement, meaning innovation, in the upper light. Instead, the part that the emanated being receives from the upper light (like lighting a candle from another without the first lessening) is what becomes “innovated” and multiplies according to the new forms in the vessels, where each one receives according to the measure of the desire in it, whose states change from one another and cascade from one another immeasurably and endlessly. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 2, item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 65:1
items.html: (to question) See Inner Observation, page 19, the passage beginning “Now”; page 20; and page 24, the passage beginning “And now.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 66:1
items.html: (to question) The screen, which is a detaining force that was placed on phase four after the restriction to prevent her from receiving inside, caused the emergence of the line from Ein Sof, since the upper light is never subject to change, and shines after the restriction as it did before the restriction. However, now the above-mentioned screen caused the upper light to be received only in the three phases of the desire, whose measure is very small compared to the reception in phase four in Ein Sof. For that reason, it received only a thin line of light, compared to the measure of the light in Ein Sof. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 2, item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 67:1
items.html: (to question) Although phase four in Ein Sof restricted herself, there is no issue of taking off a form or putting on a form after the departure of the first, as it is in corporeality. Instead, there is an issue of a new form that is added to the first, without the first form changing whatsoever, as there is not absence in anything spiritual. Thus, this entire innovation of the departure of the light and the detaining force that was performed in phase four not to receive within her is regarded as another world, new and distinguished in itself. It is added to the light of Ein Sof, which remained as it was without any change. You should infer from that regarding every new form in spirituality. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 2, item 1)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 68:1
items.html: (to question) From the coming of the line from Ein Sof, which the screen detained from shining in phase four, the coarseness in her became apparent, since she remained without light. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 2, item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 69:1
items.html: (to question) First, the light from the Emanator expands as light of Hochma, which is the general vitality that belongs to that emanated being. Inside it there is phase one in the will to receive, called the “first expansion” or “phase one.” Afterwards, the will to bestow intensifies in that light, and the intensification of that light draws light of Hassadim from the Emanator. This is called the “first intensification,” or “phase two.” Afterwards, that light of Hassadim expands a great expansion, namely with illumination of Hochma. This is called the “second expansion” or “phase three.” After that the will to receive that is included in the light from the first expansion intensifies and completes the measure of the will to receive. This is called the “second intensification” or “phase four.” (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 70:1
items.html: (to question) The Yod of HaVaYaH is the first expansion of the light, called phase one (see item 69). The first Hey of HaVaYaH is the first intensification in the light, called “phase two.” The Vav of HaVaYaH is the second expansion of the light, called “phase three,” and the last Hey of HaVaYaH is the second intensification in the light, called “phase four.” (Inner Observation, item 31, the passage beginning “And this is the secret”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 71:1
items.html: (to question) See item 49.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 72:1
items.html: (to question) It is the thought “to delight His created beings.” (Inner Observation, item 22, the passage beginning “And now”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 73:1
items.html: (to question) Everything discussed in the wisdom of Kabbalah concerns only the expansion of the light from His self; however, regarding His self, we have no utterance, word, or vessel. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 2)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 74:1
items.html: (to question) The first rudiment is that the entire reality before us is already set and exists in Ein Sof in its utter perfection. This is called the “light of Ein Sof.” The second rudiment is the five worlds called Adam Kadmon, Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira, Assiya, which cascade from Malchut of Ein Sof after the restriction. Anything that exists in the second rudiment is extended from the first rudiment. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 3, and Inner Observation, item 5, the passage beginning “And indeed”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 75:1
items.html: (to question) “He” indicates the light in Ein Sof. “His name” indicates the will to receive in Ein Sof, called Malchut of Ein Sof. “One” indicates that no disparity of form whatsoever is detected there between the light, which is “He,” and the vessel, which is “His Name.” Rather, it is all light. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 30, the passage beginning “And according to,” and Inner Observation, item 13, the passage beginning “However”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 76:1
items.html: (to question) Before the restriction, He is called Ein Sof, to indicate that there is no depiction of Sof or Sium (end) there at all, since phase four receives the light, as well. Thus, in that place, there is no reason to stop the light and form a Sof and Sium. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 20)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 77:1
items.html: (to question) The creation of the worlds and their entire contents. He restricted Himself in phase four in Him in order to reveal these worlds down to this world, where it is possible to turn the form of reception into a form of bestowal. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90, and Inner Observation, item 17, the passage beginning “And by this”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 78:1
items.html: (to question) Malchut of Ein Sof regarded the equivalence of form with her Maker as embellishment, which could only be achieved by the creation of the worlds. This is why she restricted herself. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 40 and Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 79:1
items.html: (to question) Reception only because it gives contentment to the giver. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90, the passage beginning “The restriction”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 80:1
items.html: (to question) To turn the form of reception into the form of bestowal. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 81:1
items.html: (to question) See Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 40, and Inner Observation, item 22, the passage beginning “And now.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 82:1
items.html: (to question) The restriction was not because of the disparity of form that appeared in the will to receive that wanted to correct it. It was only because of the embellishment, without any necessity and coercion.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 83:1
items.html: (to question) Because there is no “some” [part] in spirituality. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 70)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 84:1
items.html: (to question) Before the illumination of the line, phase four herself was still not regarded as coarse and low (see item 83). Hence, there is no matter of the degrees being imprinted for her. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 85:1
items.html: (to question) Because the restriction did not occur due to a disparity of form. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 86:1
items.html: (to question) Only phase four. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 2, item 3)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 87:1
items.html: (to question) When the vessels of reception acquire the form of bestowal. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 40)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 88:1
items.html: (to question) The will that is necessarily there, had a desire to embellish itself and resemble the form of the light completely, and that became the “cause” for the creation of the worlds. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 89:1
items.html: (to question) To make the vessels of reception work in order to bestow. (Inner Observation, item 22)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 90:1
items.html: (to question) Their special quality is specifically to turn the form of reception into bestowal. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 90)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 91:1
items.html: (to question) By laboring in Torah and good deeds. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 40)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 92:1
items.html: (to question) When the vessels of reception are restored to the form of bestowal. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 40, the passage beginning “restricted”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 93:1
items.html: (to question) The “teeth of form” found in the will to receive from the Emanator. (Inner Observation, item 18, the passage beginning “Know”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 94:1
items.html: (to question) Corruption and correction in the same carrier exist only in this world. (Inner Observation, item 20, the passage beginning “And by this”)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 95:1
items.html: (to question) Light of Hochma and light of Hassadim. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 96:1
items.html: (to question) The will to bestow and the will to receive. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 97:1
items.html: (to question) Light of Hassadim. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 98:1
items.html: (to question) Light of Hochma and light of Hassadim. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 99:1
items.html: (to question) Because it is extended by the intensification of the desire of the emanated being. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 100:1
items.html: (to question) After the revelation of phase four in the desire, which is the Gadlut [greatness/adulthood] of the will to receive. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 101:1
items.html: (to question) The one that receives within can only hold a limited amount of light, according to the size of the vessel. For one that receives without, the vessel does not limit the light that it holds, and it is without a limit. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 50)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 102:1
items.html: (to question) When there is no differentiation of above and below among the four phases in the desire, they are regarded as four circles one within the other, like onionskins. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 100)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 103:1
items.html: (to question) Because the restriction did not occur because of the inferiority of the disparity of form. (Inner Light, Part 1, Chapter 1, item 100)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 104:1
items.html: (to question) There is no inferiority in it by the nature of its creation, nor would any inferiority have been revealed in it had the restriction not been upon it. (Inner Observation, item 19, the passage beginning “Indeed”; see item 106.)

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 105:1
items.html: See Inner Observation, item 19, the passage beginning “Indeed.”

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section I, List of Answers on Topics 105:2
items.html: (to question) Part One completed, with God’s help.
